title: Local Services SaaS
subtitle: Build recurring revenue without drowning in onboarding, collections, channel conflict, and support.
description: Serve fragmented local operators with visible pain, tight budgets, seasonal demand, uneven digital readiness, and short but noisy buying processes. Revenue can arrive early, but failed collections, high-touch onboarding, channel economics, workforce mistakes, competitor pressure, and founder support can erase margin and hide churn risk.
learningObjectives: Distinguish software retention from founder service

problems.title: Every prospect describes a different workflow
problems.summary: The market is accessible but may be too heterogeneous for one product.
hypotheses: One trade has repeatable scheduling pain
Payment collection is the shared bottleneck
The market is too fragmented for SaaS

problems.title: Manual onboarding may erase gross margin
problems.summary: Each account needs imports, configuration, training, and founder intervention.
hypotheses: A template can eliminate most setup
The customer should pay an onboarding fee
The product targets the wrong system of record

problems.title: Interest disappears when price is discussed
problems.summary: Usage interest is not yet backed by credible budget evidence or reliable payment behavior.
hypotheses: The buyer expects a consumer price
The workflow is annoying but not costly

problems.title: Founder support is becoming the product
problems.summary: High-touch help creates retention while hiding standalone software value.
hypotheses: The founder is overpromising custom workflows

problems.title: Booked revenue is not reliable cash
problems.summary: Seasonality, payment failure, fragmented buyers, and support disputes can make growth worsen liquidity.
hypotheses: A denser local channel lowers collection cost
The segment cannot support the service burden
